title: AreaRegistry
description: The declared registry of ONE Area (ADR 0002: Company -> Area -> Process -> Capture): its identity, its responsible owner, and the declared entries of its process inventory. Complements the derived read-path (areas.list_areas projects Areas out of captured sessions): the registry is where an Area exists BEFORE anyone records into it — minted by adopting BDM domains or created manually — and where ownership lives. The effective process inventory a caller sees is the merge of these declared entries with the emergent processes derived from capture segments (process.id) and process:-tagged L4 artifacts; coverage flags (captured / has-L4 / automated) are DERIVED at read time, never stored here, so the registry cannot drift from the facts. One registry document per Area, persisted as a tagged Storage File (jazz-area-registry + area:<areaId>), replaced-not-appended on save.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the area-registry schema this document was written against, e.g. "1". Absent means "1" (every document persisted before versioning existed). Bump the MAJOR only when a breaking change lands. Readers must accept absent plus any version they can interpret, and surface — never crash on — versions they cannot.

areaId.description: Stable slug identity of the Area — the same value stamped on captures as the area.id OTLP attribute and on artifacts as the area:<id> Storage-File tag. Never renamed (rename changes the display name, not the id).

description.description: One-paragraph summary of what this slice of the company covers.

owner.description: WHO IS RESPONSIBLE for this Area — the person accountable for its model and processes (vision step 2). Optional: an Area can exist unowned until the ownership pass of the BDM interview (or a human) assigns one.

source.description: Where this Area came from, when it was minted by adopting a BDM domain grouping (the conversation is the source of the area structure). Absent for manually created Areas and for the read-time General default (which is never persisted).

kind.description: bdm-domain = adopted from a persisted domain grouping; manual = created by hand.

sessionId.description: The BDM workshop session whose domain grouping was adopted.

domainId.description: The id of the adopted domain within that grouping.

processes.description: The DECLARED process-inventory entries of this Area (ADR 0002: an Area owns one process inventory; a Process belongs to exactly one Area). Declared entries come from the interview's process-mining pass ('name the key processes in this domain'), from adopting labels, or from manual curation — they exist so the inventory can be populated BEFORE recording starts and so each process can carry an owner. Emergent processes (capture segments / L4 tags) merge with these at read time by processId.

updatedBy.description: Email of the identity that last saved the registry (attribution, mirrors savedBy elsewhere).

email.description: The responsible person's email — the join key to capture attribution (enduser.id) and OIDC identity (X-Kbc-User-Email). Optional when only a spoken name was captured (the interview often hears 'Jana from finance'); backfill the email to make the owner joinable.

assignedBy.description: Email of who made the assignment (the interviewer's authenticated identity, or the interviewee as captured in conversation).

processId.description: Stable slug identity — the same value stamped on capture segments as the process.id OTLP attribute and on artifacts as the process:<id> Storage-File tag. The join key that ties the inventory entry to its recordings, L4 doc and materialized flow.

description.description: What the process does, in the owner's words where possible.

owner.description: WHO performs / is responsible for this process — the person asked to record it (vision step 4). Defaults to the Area owner when absent.

source.description: How the entry was declared: interview = mined from the BDM conversation's process pass; label = promoted from a free-text capture label; manual = typed into the inventory UI.

conceptIds.description: Ontology concept ids this process touches (the ontology->process edge, vision step 5). Filled by the concept-linking pass over the process's L4 doc; advisory until then.

sourceSessions.description: Capture session ids known to demonstrate this process (grows as owners record).

scoring.description: The process's Operating Picture scoring (docs/design/operating-picture.md): annual impact in dollars, an operational health score, and the DERIVED verdict that ranks it on the buyer's dashboard. Optional: a process exists (and is honest about being unscored) until an owner or the AI estimator scores it.

Impact x health scoring of one process (Operating Picture S1). Every number is explicit about its source (manual = the owner typed it; ai = estimated from L4 evidence) — the dashboard shows the breakdown on demand instead of pretending precision (ADR 0001 evidence-honesty adapted to dollars).

impact.description: Annual dollar impact, split into its three components so the total is never an unexplained number.

costSavedAnnual.description: USD/yr of manual labour the process burns today — what redesign or automation would save.

revenueImpactAnnual.description: USD/yr gained or protected (cycle time, conversion, leakage stopped).

riskExposureAnnual.description: USD/yr of error / audit / key-person exposure the process carries.

totalAnnual.description: DERIVED: the sum of the three components, recomputed on every write — never client-set.

note.description: Where the numbers come from, in the scorer's words (the evidence trail behind the dollars).

health.description: How reliably the process runs today, with the observed factors that drag it down.

score.description: Operational health in [0,1]: 1 = runs itself, 0 = breaks weekly. Compared against the 0.5 threshold on the verdict's health axis.

factors.description: The observed drags on health — each one names WHY the score is what it is, grounded in what capture / the owner actually saw.

factor.description: singleOwner = one person holds it (the key-person-risk KPI counts these); manualSteps = human copy/paste work; exceptionsHeavy = the unhappy path dominates; fragileTooling = spreadsheets/scripts held together with tape; undocumented = the doc is in someone's head; other = anything else (explain in note).

note.description: The specific observation behind the factor, e.g. 'only Ingrid knows the carry-over rules'.

manualHoursAnnual.description: Hours/yr of human effort the process consumes — feeds the org-level manual-effort KPI.

verdict.description: DERIVED, never hand-set: the impact x health quadrant. Impact axis = totalAnnual vs the median over the scored set; health axis = score vs 0.5. high+unhealthy = fixFirst, low+unhealthy = automate, high+healthy = protectScale, low+healthy = watch. Recomputed across the set on every scoring write.

source.description: manual = the owner typed the numbers; ai = estimated from L4 evidence (always labelled, always editable by the owner).

scoredBy.description: Email of the identity that last wrote the scoring (server-stamped).

scoredAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last scoring write (server-stamped).
